title: Weigh an infant manikin on a beam scale: set the kilogram notch, then slide the gram weight until the pointer is level
instruction: Weigh the infant manikin on the beam scale. Move the large sliding weight one notch at a time until the beam tips down, then back one notch. Then slide the small weight along its bar until the red pointer floats level with the black counterpointer, and let go of both weights.
context: Nurses, midwives and community health workers weigh infants this way. The seca 725 mechanical baby scale's instructions for use (https://www.seca.com/fileadmin/documents/manual/seca_man_725_745_int_DE_EN_FR_IT_ES_PT_PL.pdf), "Weighing": "Move the large sliding weight until pointer and counterpointer are at approximately the same level", then "Move the small sliding weight until pointer and counterpointer are at exactly the same level", and "If you touch the scale, weight will not be measured correctly." The reading is the kilograms on the large weight plus the grams on the small one. A wrong weight misleads growth monitoring and weight-based drug doses. Done by: nurses, midwives, community health workers.
setup: Positions in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. A white plastic mechanical baby scale, 55.2 cm long (along x, from x 5.4 to 60.6), 31.2 cm deep (from y -20 to 11.2) and up to 17 cm tall, fixed. Its steel weighing beam runs along x on the scale's right side: it pivots at x 18, y -17, 11 cm above the table, and rocks 1.2 degrees either way between stops. Past the pivot, two steel bars 8 by 6 mm run from x 19.5 to 46.5, their axes 9.6 cm above the table. The inner bar, at y -14.8, carries the large sliding weight, which sits in notches (pairs of 2 mm round bars across the bar's top): 0 kg at x 21, then one every 1.5 cm to 16 kg at x 45. The outer bar, at y -19.2, carries the small sliding weight: 0 g at x 21 to 1,000 g at x 46. The large weight: a black steel sleeve 13 by 12 mm around its bar with a grey tab 8 by 8 mm and 13 mm tall on top, 400 g. The small weight: a black steel sleeve 12 by 10 mm with a grey tab 6 by 6 mm and 12 mm tall, 24 g. Both start at 0. A steel counterweight 4 by 4 cm sits on the beam's short arm at x 10. At the beam's far end, a red pointer; beside it, from x 49.2 to 50.8, a fixed black counterpointer at the pointer's height when the beam is level. Left of the beam, a white plastic tray 52 by 22 cm, its top 15.4 cm above the table, from x 7 to 59 and y -11 to 11, resting on a knife edge on the beam's short arm 6 mm from the pivot. In the tray, a 3.62 kg vinyl infant training manikin, 39 cm long, lying along x with its head away from the arms.
scoring: The reading is the large weight's notch in kg plus the small weight's place on its bar (0 to 1,000 g over 25 cm), measured at the weights' centres: it is what the beam balances. The large weight sits in a notch when its centre is within 1 mm of the notch along the bar and it is lifted no more than 0.8 mm. Not sitting in a notch: 0. In the 3 kg notch, reading more than 100 g from the manikin's 3.62 kg: 0.25. Within 100 g: 0.5. Within 40 g: 0.75. Within 20 g, with the beam floating clear of both stops and both weights still (under 1 cm/s): 0.9, and 1.0 once that has held for 1 s (the trial then ends). A wrong notch is at least 380 g off and scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 1.0. To check a real trial: read the two weights, compare with the manikin's mass, and photograph the pointer against the counterpointer.
reset_notes: Slide both weights back to 0, the large one into its 0 notch.
fidelity: The tray rests on a frictionless knife edge on the beam's short arm; a real scale carries it on a lever linkage. The large weight's notches are two round bars that cradle a key under it, and it lifts 2.5 mm to move (a real one is pulled forward to release it). No beam lock or tare screw. The weights' masses and the bars' spacing follow from the lever ratio, not seca drawings. The manikin is fixed in the tray.
